changes.old: He came to what was His own, and His own did not receive Him.
changes.new: He came to what was His own, and His own people did not receive Him.
changes.reason: The first own is neuter plural, the second masculine plural. What was His own leaves the domain broad; people makes the second form’s personal reference audible. No possession or group is narrowed to a specific place or population in the translation.

changes.old: But as many as received Him, He gave them authority to become children of God—to those who believe in His name,
changes.new: But to all who received Him, He gave authority to become children of God—to those who believe in His name,
changes.reason: To all who is a natural dative recipient construction absorbing the resumptive to them. Authority retains exousia and avoids reducing it to physical power. The apposition identifies the recipients as those believing in His name. The participle does not, by itself, prove a theory of uninterrupted belief.

changes.old: who were born not from bloods, nor from the will of flesh, nor from the will of a man, but from God.
changes.new: who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of a man, but of God.
changes.reason: The relative and passive verb are plural, referring back to the recipients in verse 12. The Greek blood noun is plural; blood is the natural English mass-noun rendering here, with the literal plurality retained in the close draft and note. The verse contrasts human generation and God as source. Do not insert a biological mechanism or read the plural as proof of two parental bloodstreams.

changes.old: John bears witness concerning Him and has cried out, saying, “This was He of whom I said, ‘The One coming after me has come before me, because He was before me.’”
changes.new: John bears witness concerning Him and has cried out, saying, “This was He of whom I said, ‘The One who comes after me has taken precedence over me, because He was before me.’”
changes.reason: The present bears witness and perfect has cried out remain. The candidate distinguishes coming later from precedence and prior existence. Taken precedence interprets emprosthen with gegonen as status; the following because-clause retains was before me. This is a proposed contextual clarification, not a claim that Greek has a separate word rank.

changes.old: For from His fullness we all received, and grace in place of grace.
changes.new: For from His fullness we all received, even grace in place of grace.
changes.reason: For renders hoti and all preserves the explicit universal within we. Even interprets kai as explanatory, specifying what was received. In place of retains the substitution/succession force of anti. The referents of the two graces are not named in this verse; do not insert a law-versus-gospel formula.

changes.old: No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten God, who is in the bosom of the Father, He has made Him known.
changes.new: No one has ever seen God; the Only-begotten God, who is in the bosom of the Father, has made Him known.
changes.reason: The selected NA28 running text reads God, not Son, at this point. The open SBL comparison apparatus also prints God and reports the Son reading in its RP comparison edition; this is edition comparison, not a fresh manuscript collation. Bosom retains the image of intimacy. The final Him is an inferred object referring to God; no explicit object is written. The resumptive that One is represented by the English subject without a second pronoun.

changes.old: This is He of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who has come before me, because He was before me.’
changes.new: This is He of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who has taken precedence over me, because He was before me.’
changes.reason: The precedence clause matches 1:15. Replace 'has come before me' with 'has taken precedence over me'; retain 'because He was before me' as the distinct ground.
